== Overview ==
The shrine originates from rituals associated with the worship of {{ill|Mount Sobo|arz|جبل مونت سوبو|ceb|Sobo-zan|fr|Mont Sobo|ja|祖母山|lld|Mont Sobo|my|ဆိုဘိုတောင်|pl|Góry Sobo|pnb|ٹلہ سوبو|vi|Núi Sobo|zh|祖母山|qid=Q3695986}}. It consists of the '''Upper shrine''' on the summit of Mount Sobo, the '''Lower shrine''' in Kanbara, Taketa, the '''Shinkōsho''' (procession site), and '''Anamori Shrine'''<ref name="170319c1" />. It is also known as '''Ubadake Daimyōjin''', '''Uha Myōjin''', and '''Sobosan Daimyōjin'''.

{{quote|Takeo Shimokorihiko Shrine<br>
Section 1: Enshrined Deity<br>
Located at Kanbara in Ubadake Village, {{ill|Naoiri District, Ōita|ja|直入郡|zh|直入郡|qid=Q6964536}}, this is an ancient shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}. {{ill|Toyotama-hime|de|Toyotama-hime|es|Toyotama-hime|fa|تویوتاما-هیمه|fi|Otohime|fr|Otohime|id|Toyotama-hime|it|Toyotama-hime|ja|トヨタマヒメ|ko|도요타마히메|mni|ꯇꯣꯌꯣꯇꯃ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Toyotama-hime|ru|Тоётама-химэ|simple|Toyotama-hime|sv|Otohime|uk|Тойотама-хіме|vi|Toyotama-hime|zh|豐玉毘賣命|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime no Mikoto}} is enshrined together with {{ill|Itsuse no Mikoto|fr|Hikoitsuse no Mikoto|ja|彦五瀬命|ko|이쓰세노미코토|pl|Itsuse|zh|彥五瀨命|qid=Q10881970}}, and it is called Takeo Shimokorihiko Shrine. It was consecrated in {{ill|Hakuchi (era)|de|Hakuchi (Ära)|es|Hakuchi (era)|fa|هاکوچی (دوره)|fr|Ère Hakuchi|hr|Hakuchi (razdoblje)|ia|Hakuchi (era)|id|Hakuchi|ja|白雉|ko|하쿠치|ru|Хакути|sh|Hakuchi (era)|simple|Hakuchi (era)|sr|Хакучи|th|ฮากูจิ (ศักราช)|tr|Hakuchi (dönem)|uk|Хакуті|zh|白雉|zh_yue|白雉|qid=Q540118}} 2 of {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|ar|الإمبراطور كوتوكو|arz|الامبراطور كوتوكو|azb|کوتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Котаку|ca|Kōtoku Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆتۆکو|cs|Kótoku|de|Kōtoku|es|Kōtoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوتوکو|fr|Kōtoku|id|Kaisar Kōtoku|it|Kōtoku|ja|孝徳天皇|ka|კოტოკუ|ko|고토쿠 천황|mr|कोतोकू|nl|Kotoku|pl|Kōtoku|pt|Kotoku|ru|Император Котоку|sh|Car Kōtoku|simple|Emperor Kōtoku|sl|Cesar Kotoku|sv|Kotoku|th|จักรพรรดิโคโตกุ|tl|Emperador Kōtoku|tr|Kōtoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Котоку|uz|Imperator Kōtoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōtoku|wuu|孝德天皇|yo|Emperor Kōtoku|zh|孝德天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôtoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|孝德天皇|qid=Q317980}}'s reign. ...|''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyokoku Shōshi}}'' (1907){{sfn|大分県|1907}}}}

== Overview of sub-shrines ==
== Upper shrine ==
This is a small shrine located on the summit of Mount Sobo. At present, no rituals are conducted at this location<ref name="170319c1" />. Note that the summit of Mount Sobo also has an upper shrine belonging to Sobodake Shrine, which is located at the foot of the mountain on the Miyazaki Prefecture side.

== Lower shrine ==
* Location: 1822 Ōaza Kanbara, Taketa, Ōita Prefecture
It is said that the shrine buildings were erected in Hakuchi 2 (650). It is also called '''Takeo Shrine''' or '''Takeo-sha'''. Together with {{ill|Takeo Shimokorihiko Shrine|ja|健男霜凝日子神社|qid=Q30935472|lt=Anamori Shrine}}, it is considered a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} for "Takeo Shimokorihiko Shrine" listed in the ''Engishiki Jinmyōchō''.

== Shinkōsho (procession site) ==
* Location: 1772 Ōaza Kanbara, Taketa, Ōita Prefecture
This was formerly a place of distant worship (yōhaijo). Dünya Savaşı|tt|Икенче бөтендөнья сугышы|tyv|Ийиги Делегей дайыны|ug|ئىككىنچى دۇنيا ئۇرۇشى|uk|Друга світова війна|ur|دوسری جنگ عظیم|uz|Ikkinchi Jahon urushi|vec|Seconda guera mondiałe|vep|Toine mail'man soda|vi|Chiến tranh thế giới thứ hai|vls|Twiddn Weireldôorloge|vo|Volakrig telid|wa|Deujhinme guere daegnrece|war|Ikaduha nga Gera han Kalibotan|wo|Ñaareelu Xareb Àdduna|wuu|第二次世界大战|xmf|მაჟირა მოსოფელიშ ლჷმა|yi|צווייטע וועלט-מלחמה|yo|Ogun Àgbáyé Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì|za|Daihngeih Baez Seiqgyaiq Dacan|zea|Twidde Weareldoôrlog|zgh|ⵉⵎⵏⵖⵉ ⴰⵎⴰⴹⵍⴰⵏ ⵡⵉⵙ ⵙⵉⵏ|zh|第二次世界大战|zh_classical|第二次世界大戰|zh_min_nan|Tē-jī-chhù Sè-kài Tāi-chiàn|zh_yue|第二次世界大戰|qid=Q362}}, the site became the center of shrine rituals as the Shinkōsho<ref>[http://www.niigata-u.com/files/oita2017/170319b1.html Takeo Shimokorihiko Shrine Shinkōsho, Kanbara, Taketa City] Ōita Hyakkei</ref>.

== Anamori Shrine ==
* Location: 1432 Ōaza Kanbara, Taketa, Ōita Prefecture
* Enshrined deity: Ubadake Daimyōjin
Behind the shrine there is a cave where the great serpent, believed to be the incarnation of Ubadake Daimyōjin, is said to have dwelt. This cave is regarded as the sacred object of worship (goshintai). The birth legend of {{ill|Ogata no Saburo Koreyoshi|fr|Ogata no Saburo Koreyoshi|ja|緒方惟栄|th|โองาตะ โนะ ซาบูโระ โคเรโยชิ|qid=Q7079849}} associated with this great serpent is also recounted in the ''{{ill|The Tale of the Heike|ar|قصة الهائيكي|ban|Heike Monogatari|ca|Heike monogatari|cs|Příběh rodu Taira|de|Heike Monogatari|es|Heike Monogatari|fa|هیکه مونوگاتاری|fi|Heike monogatari|fr|Le Dit des Heike|hu|Heike monogatari|id|Heike Monogatari|it|Heike monogatari|ja|平家物語|ko|헤이케모노가타리|pl|Heike monogatari|pt|Heike Monogatari|ru|Повесть о доме Тайра|simple|The Tale of the Heike|sv|Heike monogatari|th|ตำนานเฮเกะ|tr|Heike Monogatari|uk|Хейке моноґатарі|vi|Truyện kể Heike|zh|平家物语|zh_yue|平家物語|qid=Q830740}}'', Book Eight, in the chapter titled "Onokami" (Ogata's Lineage)<ref>[http://www.manabu-oshieru.com/daigakujuken/kobun/heike/08/0303.html Tale of the Heike - Book Eight, Onokami: "In the province of Bungo..." (Original text and modern translation)] Manabu-Oshieru.COM</ref>. There is a tradition that taking home a small stone from inside the cave will bring the blessing of children, and many visitors come to pray for success in romance and fertility<ref>[https://www.city.taketa.oita.jp/photo_news/?id=971 Photo News: The torii gate on the approach to Anamori Shrine restored to its beautiful form for the first time in 50 years!] Taketa City, August 30, 2014</ref>. The shrine was formerly also called '''Ike no Myōjin''' (Pond Deity) or '''Iwaya Daimyōjin''' (Cave Great Deity)<ref>[http://www.niigata-u.com/files/oita2017/170319a1.html Anamori Shrine, Kanbara, Taketa City] Ōita Hyakkei</ref>. Together with the {{ill|Takeo Shimokorihiko Shrine|ja|健男霜凝日子神社|qid=Q30935472|lt=Lower shrine}}, it is considered a candidate shrine for "Takeo Shimokorihiko Shrine" listed in the ''Engishiki Jinmyōchō''.
